title: WCC - Haulage of Food Waste from Warwickshire County Council Collection Points
description:
Warwickshire County Council (the Council) was seeking a Supplier who could provide a haulage service for separately collected food waste from specified collection points. Full details were outlined in the ITT

The value of £1.8 million at II.1.7 is an anticipated figure to allow for volumes of food waste tonnage across all waste collection authorities in Warwickshire. Currently food waste is only collected separately by Warwick District and Stratford-on-Avon District.  

The initial contract term will be for a period of 2 years.
However, the Council reserves the right to extend the contract by further periods not exceeding 30 months (2 years and 6 months) in total (30 months being the maximum available extension period) at the discretion of the Council. This means the maximum possible Contract term is 4 years and 6 months in total. 

Warwickshire County Council (the Council) was seeking a Supplier who could provide a collection and haulage service for separately collected food waste stored in containers from specified collection points to the Delivery Point. Full details were outlined in the ITT.

Warwickshire County Council is the Waste Disposal Authority and managed the Council's statutory obligation to provide treatment and disposal for municipal waste collected throughout Warwickshire by the Waste Collection Authorities and/or by suppliers acting on behalf of these Councils.

The Waste Collection Authorities (WCAs) in Warwickshire are: 
North Warwickshire Borough Council;
Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council;
Rugby Borough Council;
Warwick District Council;
Stratford-on-Avon District Council.

The WCAs listed above have a statutory obligation to arrange for the kerbside collection of waste from households in Warwickshire.

Warwick District Council and Stratford-on-Avon District Council carry out weekly collections of separately collected food waste.

There is currently no separately collected food waste service operating in North Warwickshire Borough Council, Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council and Rugby Borough Council. However, it is possible that North Warwickshire Borough Council, Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council and Rugby Borough Council implement separate food waste collections in the near future if this is made a requirement by Government or for other reasons. If separate food waste collections are implemented by one or all of these WCAs, the Council may require a collection and haulage service for this material. Details were outlined in the ITT. These additional services will not necessarily run for the full term of the contract (4 years and 6 months) and will instead run on a co-terminus basis with the services for Warwick District Council and Stratford-on-Avon District Council.

title: WCC - Reprocessing of Separately Collected Food Waste
description:
Warwickshire County Council is a waste disposal authority and is seeking to appoint a Supplier for the reprocessing of separately collected Food Waste.

The initial contract term will be for a period of 5 years. However, the Council reserves the right to extend the Contract by further periods not exceeding 60 months (5 years) in total. The maximum contract term will be 120 months (10 years). 

The Council is procuring the following lots/options:
• Lot 1 - Reprocessing of separately collected Food Waste for the whole of the Warwickshire County (all five Warwickshire Waste Collection Authorities);
• Lot 2 - Reprocessing of separately collected Food Waste from the following two Waste Collection Authorities - Warwick District Council and Stratford-on-Avon District Council;
• Lot 3 - Reprocessing of separately collected Food Waste from the following three Waste Collection Authorities - North Warwickshire Borough Council, Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council and Rugby Borough Council.

Please note that there is currently no separately collected Food Waste service  operating in North Warwickshire Borough Council, Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council and Rugby Borough Council. Therefore please note Lot 3 and the additional services in Lot 1 will not necessarily be a 10 year contract and will run on a co-terminus basis with the services for Warwick District Council and Stratford-on-Avon District Council from the point at which it starts.

All applicants must tender for all 3 Lots/options.
For the avoidance of doubt, if an applicant doesn't submit a tender for all 3 of the Lots/Options, their submission will be rejected and will not proceed to evaluation.

It is the Council's preference to award to a single Supplier via Lot 1/Option 1 for the reprocessing of food waste for the whole of Warwickshire; however, the Council reserve the right to award the Contract as two separate Lots/Options (Lot/Option 2)and (Lot/Option 3)) at its absolute sole discretion. This may be for reasons(including but not limited to) that the awarding of this Contract as two separate Lots/Options provides significantly better value to the Council in terms of the overall annual service cost compared to Lot/Option 1. However, even where this is the case, bidders are reminded that our preference is to award Lot 1/Option 1, and the Council's decision will be final.
Further detail can be found in the ITT.

title: WCC - Container provision, haulage and reprocessing of Wood Waste from Warwickshire Household Waste Recycling Centres
description:
Warwickshire County Council (the Council) is seeking a Supplier who can provide containers, along with a haulage and reprocessing service for Wood Waste from specified Warwickshire Household Waste Recycling Centres (HWRCs). Full details provided in the ITT.

It is the responsibility of Warwickshire County Council, as the Waste Disposal Authority to provide HWRCs for members of the public. The Waste Collection Authorities in Warwickshire are as follows: Warwick District Council, Stratford-on-Avon District Council, North Warwickshire Borough Council, Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council, Rugby Borough Council.

The waste from the HWRCs needs to be managed safely and in line with the waste hierarchy. The Council manages 8 of its HWRCs in-house and must have contracts in place for the reuse, recycling, recovery or disposal of waste materials brought to the site by the public or traders. One of the waste materials the Council needs to have a contract for is Wood Waste. In 2022/23 the amount of Wood Waste arising from all 9 Warwickshire HWRCs was approximately 8,000 tonnes (approximately 6,500 tonnes was from 8 of the Warwickshire operated HWRCs and approximately 1,500 was from Judkins HWRC). Wood Waste arising from Judkins HWRC located in Nuneaton, is operated by FCC Environment Limited ("FCC") and the reprocessing may or may not be included in the contract at the discretion of FCC and consent of the Council. If it is included, they do not require the provision of containers or haulage. 

The initial contract term will be for a period of 3 years.
However, the Council reserves the right to extend the contract by further periods not exceeding 48 months (4 years) in total at the discretion of the Council.

title: Inductive Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectrometry - AWARD
description:
The University of Warwick has a requirement to purchase an inductive coupled plasma optical emission spectrometer (ICP-OES) for trace element analysis. 
      
      A high performance ICP-OES system is required to replace our existing obsolete ICP-OES system to carry out metal/semi-metal elements quantitation analysis in the Department of Chemistry (University of Warwick). The instrument will be used primarily for the analysis of complex samples with a variety of background/matrix from biological and synthetic studies. Due to extremely low metal content in many biological samples and very large concentration range observed, high sensitivity (low ppb (<10) for majority of metal elements) and high dynamic range are essential. The ability to handle high matrix content in sample introduction and an auto-sampler that can accommodate different sample vials (from 2ml to 50ml, tray that can load up to 200 samples) are also required.

title: Financial Transactions & Survey Data (Gambling Commission)
description:
We seek to procure an anonymous dataset of categorized banking transactions from a panel of individuals in Great Britain. This data should include all the financial transactions of each individual, across all of their accounts. It should also include demographic markers including, but not necessarily limited to, age, gender, ethnic origin, and region. Additionally, this contract will include the delivery of two surveys per year to a sample of individuals in the data. These surveys will be designed by our project team but will be implemented and delivered by the chosen supplier.

The panel should be large enough for us to undertake granular analysis of subgroups of the population determined by their demographics or behaviours. It should also be large enough to capture a meaningfully large number of individuals who may be at risk of, or suffering from, gambling-related harm. It must be as close to demographically representative as possible and include significant numbers of both gamblers and non-gamblers. 

We are seeking recent, as well as ongoing, data for the length of the contract. We expect to receive an initial transfer of transactional data at the beginning of the contract comprising historical data up to that date. This will be followed by regular updates of data for all individuals on the panel. We require access to the data for our own analysts, as well as for a limited set of researchers at the University of Warwick with whom we have an existing collaboration agreement, for the purpose of delivering the objectives of that agreement. The academics at the University of Warwick will not use the data to conduct analyses unconnected to their collaboration agreement with the Commission. The data will be held securely and analysed at the Commission as well as at Warwick. We require no training, data analytics or visualization tools. 

We intend to use the data to provide evidence for policy definition and evaluation, as well as for market tracking and insight.  We will communicate this evidence both internally, within the Commission, and externally. This will include presentations at conferences as well as the publication of results from our analyses on the Commission website and in international academic journals.

title: Electron Diffraction Instrument
description:
The University of Southampton and the University of Warwick have a requirement to
each purchase a dedicated electron diffractometer for high-throughput structural
solution (two diffractometers in total) using Electron Diffraction. These
instruments will form part of a national facility in conjunction with the national
crystallographic service at Southampton. This procurement will be funded under an
Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC) grant with the aim of
kickstarting the widespread usage of electron diffraction by the crystallographic
community within the UK. 
The instruments will sit alongside and integrate with our existing and extensive XRay diffraction facilities. To that end the instruments must be suitable for use by
non-specialist microscopists and should allow for the high-throughput collection of
data for structural solution. Equally, the software must also be easy to use and
allow for merging of datasets from multiple crystals to ensure sufficient
completeness for publication.
Alongside the national aspect, there will be local users from both universities
spanning a large range of different areas of materials research. There will also be
technique development, with regards to optimised sample preparation, new classes
of materials, but also on areas such as improving the refinements, e.g., dynamical
diffraction. It is hoped to work with the successful supplier to develop this for the
good of the whole community.
This tender is being run as a further competition against the NWUPC High Value
Laboratory Equipment Lot 10 Polycrystalline & Single Crystal X-Ray Analysis
(LAB3123 NW)
With reference to the joint procurement, the University of Southampton will be
responsible for running the Further Competition process via its e-tendering portal,
receiving and responding to general project correspondence and clarification
requests, receiving the Further Competition responses, co-ordinating and
facilitating the tender evaluation and moderation and awarding the eventual
contract. Following formal contract award, the two institutions will be responsible
for forming their own contracts. 
The successful supplier will be contracting with two separate institutions, the
University of Southampton and the University of Warwick. Each institution will have
its own contract with the successful supplier, will stipulate separate delivery and
installation locations and instructions, will require separate invoices and will raise
separate purchase orders. 
The final award of this contract will be subject to funding being approved, if the
funds are not approved, we reserve the right to not award a contract as a result of
this Further Competition process.

title: COV - Transport and Infrastructure Research & Development (R&D) Partner - AWARD
description:
Coventry City Council ("the Council") has opted to run a Competitive Dialogue procedure under the Utilities Contracts Regulations 2016 and is seeking to appoint a framework of Research & Development (R&D) partners.
      
      The Council has been and will continue to develop the living and working environment within Coventry through a series of programmes that improve the transport infrastructure to attract inward investment and drive the transition from fossil fuel transport to sustainable transportation solutions.
       
      One key project in this drive for modal shift is the Coventry Very Light Rail (VLR) project. This project is to develop a VLR product that can be manufactured predominantly in the West Midlands that will drive modal shift within small to medium size urban environments, consistent with many cities within the UK where a standard tram system would not be economically feasible. 
      
      This system will be a low capital cost for installation and will be environmentally clean at the point of use, which will have a positive impact on air quality, this modal shift is designed to reduce congestion, and as a result, open up the city for investment especially along the route.
      
      The approach that the Council has taken to achieve the ambition outlined above is one of innovation and development. This framework of R&D Partners is to develop relationships with organisations that can support all phases of product development from ideation through to market ready product. 
      
      It is understood that any R&D Partner will need to be able to exercise a support framework of subcontractors and suppliers to achieve the service offering of the full technology development cycle.
      
      The Council seeks to appoint a framework of up to six (6) research and development partners to provide associated services .
